Stages are the playing fields where the player fights off hordes of enemies to survive as long as possible until the stage's time limit is reached.

The game currently features 81 stages, divided into 34 primary stages and 47 Adventure Mode-exclusive stages. The primary stages consist of 20 base-game stages and 10 DLC-exclusive stages. The 20 base game stages comprise 5 normal stages, 7 bonus stages, 9 challenge stages, 2 special stages, and 1 hidden stage. Adventure Mode includes 18 base game stages and 41 stages across all DLC adventures, including Planar Bazaar, which is shared by all adventures and counted as a single stage.
Stages are unlocked by meeting specific requirements associated with their corresponding achievements and do not need to be purchased with coins. The only exception is
, which is unlocked by default as the first playable stage.

In the mobile version, players who fail to complete a stage may be offered the option to watch an advertisement in exchange for one Revival. Additionally, players may be offered the option to watch an advertisement for extra gold upon reaching the results screen.
Stage Selection menu
The Stage Selection menu becomes accessible after the player selects a character in the Character Selection menu and unlocks
, the game's second stage. Before Inlaid Library is unlocked, selecting a character takes the player directly to
. The menu displays a list of available stages, along with information about each stage, and allows players to activate unlocked modifiers before starting a run.
The following sections describe the other features found in the Stage Selection menu.
Stage modifiers window

Each stage applies modifiers to certain player and enemy stats. In addition to a stage's base modifiers, extra modifiers can be applied by enabling modes. These modifiers can affect the player's movement speed, projectile speed, gold gain, and luck, as well as enemy movement speed, health, damage, and quantity.

The bonuses from a stage's base modifiers and enabled modes stack additively. The resulting bonus is then applied as a multiplier to the corresponding stat bonuses from passive items and PowerUps. These stage modifiers are separate from their corresponding player stats, such as gold bonus and
, or movement speed bonus and
. Similarly, enemy health, movement speed, and damage modifiers are separate from

For example, a stage with a base gold bonus of +25% and an additional +200% bonus from Inverse Mode has a combined gold bonus of +225%, equivalent to a 3.25× multiplier. A character with +300% Greed has a total Greed multiplier of 4×, including the base value of 100%. A
Rich Coin Bag, which normally grants 100 gold coins, therefore grants 1,300 coins under these conditions (100 × 4 × 3.25).
Luck is the exception to this rule, as stage and mode Luck bonuses are added directly to the character's
stat rather than applied as a multiplier.
Modes and gameplay modifiers window

Modes and gameplay modifiers are options that alter gameplay inside a stage. Modes adjust various player and enemy stats or change the stage's rules, while gameplay modifiers introduce additional mechanics or modify existing ones.

The game features four unlockable modes: Hyper, Hurry, Inverse, and Endless. It also features four unlockable gameplay modifiers: Arcanas, Limit Break, and the two Randomizers, which consist of Random Events and Random LevelUp.

Modes and gameplay modifiers can be activated before starting a stage through the Stage Selection menu. Multiple options can be enabled at the same time, allowing players to combine them for different gameplay experiences.

Certain stages restrict the use of modes and gameplay modifiers. In Eudaimonia Machine and Room 1665, Hyper Mode, Hurry Mode, Inverse Mode, Endless Mode, and Random Events cannot be enabled and are automatically disabled upon entering the stage if previously activated. Additionally, Arcanas are disabled in Eudaimonia Machine. In Room 1665, Arcanas can only be obtained from the stage's pre-placed
Arcana chests, whether Arcanas are toggled on or off.
Hyper Mode

Hyper Mode adds a +65%–75% bonus to the movement speed of the character and enemies, a +15%–25% bonus to projectile speed, and a +50% bonus to gold gain. Depending on the stage, it may also grant bonuses to the player's

and enemy health and their minimum spawn count. The exact bonuses vary between stages and are displayed in the Stage Modifiers window. The overall bonuses granted by hyper mode differ with each stage, the values of which are displayed on the Stage Modifiers window.
In Normal stages including the DLCs, Hyper Mode is unlocked by defeating the 25:00 boss of the stage with the exception of

. In all other stages types (Challenge, Bonus), Hyper Mode is unlocked automatically when the stage itself is unlocked.

Hurry Mode
Hurry Mode doubles the stage's Clock Speed and grants a +25% bonus to XP gain. This bonus is applied independently of the player's
stat, which acts as a separate multiplier for XP gain.

The increased Clock Speed causes the in-game timer to advance twice as fast, halving the real-time duration required to reach the stage's time limit. Time-based events, such as enemy spawns, evolution chest drops, and wave events, still occur at their usual timestamps on the in-game timer, just twice as earlier.

Endless Mode
Endless Mode prevents

Reapers from spawning when the stage's time limit is reached. Instead, the enemy waves restart from the beginning, completing a cycle and allowing the run to continue indefinitely. The stage is considered cleared and complete after the first cycle. With each subsequent cycle, enemies gain +100% of their base HP, their spawn frequency and quantity increase by 50%, their damage dealt increases by 25%, and the player's maximum incoming damage cap decreases by 1.
In Endless Mode, the Merchant reappears after each cycle and offers one additional

Death still have their runs end and automatically disappear when the stage's time limit is reached, even with Endless Mode enabled.

Arcana
The Arcanas are a set of individual modifiers styled after tarot cards, each with its own set of effects and changes to certain aspects of gameplay.

With Arcanas activated, the player can obtain three of them throughout a run, the first of which is given at the start of the run and the other two from Arcana chests dropped by special bosses at specific timestamps. Although only three Arcanas can normally be possessed simultaneously, the player can have an unlimited number of Arcanas. Limit Break
Limit Break enables equipped weapons to be upgraded beyond their usual limits, allowing weapons to become more powerful than what they normally are.

With Limit Break activated, upon maxing out all equipped weapon and passive items, the player will no longer receive Coin or Floor Chicken options. Instead, they will start to receive Limit Break upgrades, with each level-up providing an upgrade to a specific stat for one of the player's equipped weapons.

Randomizers
Randomizers window

Randomizers are special gameplay options which adds a factor of unpredictability to the gameplay, as their name implies. Unlike other modifiers which is intended to directly enhance gameplay, Randomizers focus on increasing stage difficulty by incorporating an element of randomness to each run.

Currently, the game features two Randomizers: Random Events and Random LevelUp. These options can be accessed through a dedicated window in the Stage Selection screen, located alongside the windows for modes and other gameplay modifiers. Notably, this Randomizers window is not visible initially and only becomes available after unlocking at least one Randomizer.
Random Events

Random Events, also referred to as Randomized Minute Events, introduce a spinning roulette to the bottom-right corner of the screen when activated before a run, which appears as The Directer's masks on three black concentric rings. At the 30-second mark of every minute, the roulette selects a random event, which then triggers at the start of the following minute. These events vary widely in their effects—some may be beneficial, others detrimental, and some simply add a touch of humor without significant impact.
The Random Events option is unlocked by collecting the
relic, located in
. Notably, this feature is always enabled by default in Astral Stair before acquiring the Trisection relic. Once unlocked, it can be toggled on or off like other stage modifiers.
Random LevelUp

Random LevelUp, when enabled before a run, removes the player’s ability to manually select items during level-ups. Instead, the game automatically designates a random weapon or passive item to be added or upgraded in the player’s inventory. If Limit Break is also enabled, Random LevelUp will continue to apply its effects to it as well.
The Random LevelUp option is unlocked by collecting the
relic, which appears in
at the 18-minute mark.

Music Selection is a feature that allows players to customize the background music of a stage by choosing from any unlocked music tracks in the game. Players can also apply modifiers to the music, which include Normal, Hyper, and Forsaken. The Normal modifier plays the track in its original form, while Hyper increases the speed and pitch of the music, and conversely, Forsaken slows the music down and lowers its pitch.
